sections.h2: How can a house in Union be sold?
sections.html:
Owners in Broome County's Union have an agent, a do-it-yourself sale or an all-cash buyer to choose from. The notes below cover the whole town: the villages of Endicott and Johnson City, plus hamlets such as Endwell, Union Center, West Corners and Westover.

A listing can fetch the top price for a house in good shape, at the cost of showings, inspections and waiting on a buyer's mortgage. Selling for cash gives up some of that upside in return for a simpler path, which helps if you face repairs, a tenant, an inherited property or a move with a deadline.

  • Agent: the most exposure and preparation, and financing contingencies from buyers.
  • By owner: you save the commission and do all the paperwork yourself.
  • All cash: the house is bought as is and the two sides agree on a closing date.

Whatever you choose, sort out the town's paperwork first. The code office letter described below is the item to request first.

sections.h2: Where is Union and who lives there?
sections.html:
Union sits on the north side of the Susquehanna River, west of Binghamton, and is one of the communities that make up the Triple Cities along with Johnson City and Endicott. The Census Bureau estimates 53,972 residents on July 1, 2025, a 3.9 percent drop from the 2020 base of 56,161, across 35.44 square miles of land (QuickFacts).

The town was established in 1791, back when the area belonged to Tioga County, and its population climbed from 5,707 in 1900 to a peak of 64,490 in 1970. Getting around is straightforward: NY 17 crosses the river here, NY 26 and NY 38B meet near Union Center, NY 17C runs across the south, and Tri-Cities Airport sits in the southwest corner.

In the 2020 to 2024 figures, owner-occupied homes have a median value of $149,900, owners live in 58.9 percent of homes, and there are 24,963 households. Rent runs $936 at the median, household income is $61,713, and 21.4 percent of residents are past 65. Mean travel time to work is 17.7 minutes, a short commute that buyers working in Binghamton will notice.

sections.h2: How are Union homes assessed and taxed?
sections.html:
The town assessor keeps tax maps for roughly 23,000 parcels, according to the assessor's page. The town is not at 100 percent assessment, so New York State issues an equalization rate each year that reflects the average ratio of assessed value to market value, based mainly on arm's-length sales from the previous year.

That matters when you read your bill. An assessed value of $120,000 does not mean the town thinks your house is worth $120,000. Ask the assessor for the current equalization rate before you compare your assessment to an offer.

Town of Union assessment calendar from the assessor
DateWhat it means
March 1Taxable status date; what is on the property that day is reflected in the July 1 roll
May 1Tentative roll presented, no changes afterward
Fourth Tuesday in MayGrievance Board meets to hear complaints
July 1Final roll takes effect and cannot change until the next July 1 except by court order

The Grievance Day page describes a three-member board that acts independently of the assessor and meets once a year. In 2027 the fourth Tuesday in May falls on May 25. The tentative roll is viewable online within the first 10 days of May.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can Union homeowners apply for, and when?
sections.html:
The Assessor's Office accepts veterans exemptions and new Enhanced STAR applications, for people turning 65 who now hold Basic STAR, between September 1 and March 1. Exemptions that depend on current income, such as the low-income senior and disability exemptions, are accepted only from January 15 to March 1.

  • New homeowners apply for STAR directly through the New York State Tax Department.
  • Enhanced STAR applicants need the prior year's income statement or tax return.
  • The town also offers a home improvement exemption, with a form on its forms page.

Because these windows fall in winter, an owner who sells in the spring should check that the exemption was filed for the current roll, and a buyer should ask the assessor which exemptions on the current bill will end at closing.

sections.h2: What do you need from the Town of Union code office before a sale?
sections.html:
The town's certificate of occupancy page says new buildings and additions need a certificate before use, and most lenders now require one before issuing a mortgage. For an existing building, the Code Enforcement Staff issues a letter stating that the building is a legal nonconforming use, and those letters are also necessary when properties are sold.

Request it early, and ask the code staff what they need to see for your address. Building permit fees, inspection rules and junk vehicle and weed rules are all posted on the town site if you need to fix an exterior problem before buyers visit.

Flood history is part of Union's story. The town's flood management page keeps recovery documents from the 2011 flooding that followed Tropical Storm Lee, including FEMA buyout program materials. If your lot is mapped in a flood zone, an insurer will ask about it, so gather elevation and insurance records before listing.

sections.h2: What does recording a Union sale involve in Broome County?
sections.html:
The Broome County Clerk records deeds at the Broome County Office Building, 60 Hawley Street in Binghamton. Its deed FAQ page lists a $45 charge plus $5 per page for the deed, $10 for the TP-584 transfer tax return and $125 for the RP-5217 on a residential property, which comes to roughly $190 for a standard two-page deed.

The clerk's page also says transfer tax in Broome County is $5 per $1,000 of price, with $4 going to the State and $1 to Broome County, and that you pay the full $5 with the return. The sale price is rounded up to the next $500 to compute it. On a $150,000 sale, that is $750 under the clerk's formula.

  • The seller signs the deed before a notary, and the names must match on the deed, TP-584 and RP-5217.
  • Both the seller and the buyer sign the TP-584 and the RP-5217.
  • Out-of-state sellers also file form IT-2663, the nonresident estimated income tax payment.
  • A recorded deed cannot be amended. Fixing an error or changing who owns the house takes a new deed, so read the draft closely before you sign.
  • Send documents as originals, not photocopies, and include a self-addressed stamped envelope for their return.
  • Deeds back to 1963 can be searched on the clerk's website, and copies are $0.65 per page at the office.

The clerk also offers a free Fraud Alert that emails you whenever a deed or mortgage is recorded under your name.

faqs.q: Are Endicott and Johnson City part of Union?
faqs.a: Yes, as villages inside the town, alongside hamlets such as Endwell, Union Center and West Corners. Confirm with the assessor which taxing jurisdictions apply to your address.

faqs.q: When does the Union Grievance Board meet?
faqs.a: On the fourth Tuesday of May, which is May 25 in 2027. A three-member board hears complaints about the tentative roll filed May 1.

faqs.q: What are the county's deed recording charges?
faqs.a: The clerk's posted charges are $45 plus $5 a page for the deed, $10 for the TP-584 and $125 for the RP-5217 on a residential parcel. A standard two-page deed totals about $190 before transfer tax.

faqs.q: Do I need a letter from the town code office to sell?
faqs.a: The town says a letter from Code Enforcement stating legal nonconforming use is necessary when properties are sold. Ask the code staff what applies to your address, especially after any conversion or unpermitted work.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Union house with flood history?
faqs.a: Yes, though you should collect records first. The town's flood management page keeps documents from the 2011 recovery, including FEMA buyout program materials, and insurers and buyers may raise the subject.
